stem: A nurse reviews a prescription for metoprolol succinate extended-release. Which statement about this formulation is accurate?

options.A: It is an extended-release formulation administered once daily as prescribed
options.B: It is the immediate-release formulation that normally requires several scheduled doses each day
options.C: Its release characteristics are identical to every metoprolol formulation, so substitutions require no review
options.D: It should routinely be crushed to convert it to immediate-release metoprolol

rationale: Current DailyMed labeling identifies metoprolol succinate as an extended-release tablet and directs once-daily administration. The label also provides a specific conversion instruction when switching from immediate-release metoprolol, so formulations should not be informally substituted or manipulated to alter release. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize that metoprolol succinate is an extended-release, once-daily formulation and avoid unsafe informal formulation substitution.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine (official FDA drug labeling)
source_locator: Highlights, Dosage and Administration section 2 — administer once daily; switching from immediate-release metoprolol
source_claim_supported: Metoprolol succinate is an extended-release formulation administered once daily; switching from immediate-release metoprolol follows labeled conversion guidance.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration and medication safety
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — extended-release medication formulations

source_original.stem: A nurse compares metoprolol succinate extended-release with immediate-release metoprolol tartrate. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: Metoprolol succinate is extended-release and is commonly administered once daily as prescribed
options.B: Metoprolol tartrate is the extended-release formulation intended only for once-daily treatment
options.C: The two formulations have identical release characteristics and can be substituted without review
options.D: Metoprolol succinate is immediate-release and normally requires more frequent scheduled dosing

source_original.rationale: Metoprolol succinate is an extended-release formulation commonly dosed once daily. Metoprolol tartrate is immediate-release and is generally dosed more frequently. Formulation changes should follow the prescribed conversion rather than informal substitution.
source_original.source_detail: Metoprolol formulation labeling: succinate extended-release versus tartrate immediate-release; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced a generic FDA label directory with a current product-specific DailyMed label and removed unnecessary dependence on a second formulation label. Simplified the item to the directly supported succinate extended-release/once-daily fact and reduced difficulty from hard to easy.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current official DailyMed label; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: A DailyMed label updated May 13, 2026 was checked on 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The label explicitly identifies extended-release metoprolol succinate and states administer once daily; it also specifies a conversion approach when switching from immediate-release metoprolol.

distractor_audit.B: Contradicts the formulation stated in the stem and label.
distractor_audit.C: Unsafe; release characteristics and conversion instructions matter.
distractor_audit.D: Contradicts extended-release status and should not be used to alter release.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: A is the only answer consistent with the current label.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed extraneous tartrate comparison and made all alternatives formulation-focused.
audit_findings.blueprint: Medication formulation and safe administration fit Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current DailyMed dosage instructions; A remains uniquely correct.
